The surah "al-Ikhlas" is Meccan according to Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah and Jabir. It is Medinan according to one of the two opinions attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, and to Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. It has four verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten.﴾ ﴿And there is none comparable to Him.﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One (aḥad)﴾, meaning the One, the Single, who has no likeness, no equal, no consort, no child and no partner. The root of aḥad is waḥad; the waw was changed into a hamzah. From this is the saying of al-Nabighah [[The first half of the line, as in his mu'allaqah:
kaʼanna rahli wa-qad zāla al-nahāru bina
and dhu al-Jalil is a place where al-Jalil grows, and al-Jalil is al-thumam. Al-thumam is a weak, short plant that does not grow tall.]]:

*bi-dhi al-Jalil ʿalā mustaʾnisin waḥadi*

The difference between wāḥid and aḥad has already been discussed in surah al-Baqarah, and it is also fully treated in the book "al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna". All praise is due to Allah. Aḥad is in the nominative, meaning: He is aḥad. It has also been said that the meaning is: Say: The matter and affair is: Allah is aḥad. It has also been said that aḥad is a substitute (badal) for the word Allah. A group of readers read (aḥadun Allahu) without tanwin, seeking lightness and to avoid the meeting of two unvoweled letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). From this is the saying of the poet:

*wa-la dhakira Allaha illa qalilan*

This is the second half of a line by Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali. Its first half is:

*fa-alfaythu ghayra mustaʿtibin*

﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge (al-samad)﴾, meaning the One to whom one turns (yusmadu ilayhi) in needs. This is what al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The One to whom one turns in needs," as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [[Verse 53 of surah al-Nahl.]] [al-Nahl: 53]. The lexicographers said: al-samad is the lord (sayyid) to whom one turns in calamities and needs. He said:

*alā bakkara al-nāʿī bi-khayri [[It is narrated as "bi-khayri", and that is the correct reading, because after it he mentions two people.]] banī Asad ... bi-ʿAmr ibn Mas'ud wa-bi-l-sayyid al-samad*

Some people said: al-samad is the one who endures and remains, who has not ceased and will not cease. It has also been said: its explanation is what follows it: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten.﴾ Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: al-samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will die, and everything that dies is inherited. Ali, Ibn 'Abbas also, Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah and Sufyan said: al-samad is the lord (sayyid) whose lordship has reached its completion in all kinds of nobility and lordship. From this is the saying of the poet:

*ʿalawtahu bi-ḥusāmin thumma qultu lahu ... khudhhā Ḥudhayf fa-anta al-sayyid al-samad*

Abu Hurayrah said: it is the One who is free of need of every creature, and every creature is in need of Him. al-Suddi said: it is the One sought in desires and the One sought for help in calamities. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the One who does what He wills and decrees what He desires. Muqatil said: it is the Perfect, in whom there is no defect, and from this is the saying of al-Zibriqan:

*sirū jamīʿan bi-niṣfi al-layli wa-iʿtamadū ... wa-lā rahīnata illā sayyidun ṣamadu*

al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Jubayr said: al-samad is the solid (al-muṣmat) which has no hollow (jawf) [[This is not permissible for Allah, the Exalted.]]. The poet said:

*shihābu ḥurūbin lā tuzālu jiyāduhu ... ʿawābisa yaʿlukna al-shakīma al-muṣammadā [[ʿalaka al-dābbatu al-lijām yaʿlukuhu (from the pattern qatala) ʿalkan: she chewed it and moved it. The kashīm and shakīmah: the iron bar across the horse's mouth.]]*

I say: We have already presented these opinions explained in the discussion of al-samad in "al-Asna", and that the correct one among them is what the derivation (ishtiqaq) supports, which is the first opinion, mentioned by al-Khattabi. Whoever Allah has removed far away and disgraced, and whose abode and dwelling He has made the Fire, has dropped from this surah, and he recited "Allah, the One, the Eternal" in the prayer while people were listening, so he dropped "Say: He is", and claimed that it is not part of the Qur'an. He altered the wording of aḥad and claimed that this is the correct version, while what the people hold is falsehood and absurdity, thereby nullifying the meaning of the verse. The people of tafsir said: the verse was revealed as an answer to the polytheists when they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Describe your Lord for us: is He of gold, or of copper, or of brass?" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, responded to them: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ So in "He is" there is an indication of the place of the response and the location of the answer. When it is dropped, the meaning of the verse collapses, and the fabrication against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the denial of His Messenger ﷺ, become valid. al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the polytheists said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Give us the lineage of your Lord," so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ And al-samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will die, and everything that dies will be inherited, whereas Allah, the Exalted, does not die and is not inherited. ﴿And there is none comparable to Him (kufuwan aḥad)﴾ [[Reading with the hamzah is the reading of Nafi', and it is the reading of the author.]]: He said: there is no likeness to Him and no equal, and there is nothing like unto Him. It is narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah that the Prophet ﷺ mentioned their gods, and they said: "Give us the lineage of your Lord." He said: Jibril then brought him this surah, "Say: He is Allah, the One," and he mentioned something similar, but he did not mention from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and this is more sound, as al-Tirmidhi said. I say: In this hadith there is confirmation of the wording "Say: He is Allah, the One" and the explanation of al-samad, which has already been mentioned. Something similar is narrated from 'Ikrimah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He begets not" as Maryam gave birth, "nor is He begotten" as 'Isa and 'Uzayr were begotten. This is a refutation of the Christians and of those who say: 'Uzayr is the son of Allah.

﴿And there is none comparable to Him (wa-lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad)﴾, meaning: there was never anyone like Him, any equal. There is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in it; its estimated form is: "wa-lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad," and he placed the predicate of kana before its subject so that the endings of the verses would follow one pattern. Kufuwan is also read with a damma on the fa' and with sukun. It has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah that every noun of three letters whose first letter is vowelled with damma may have the middle letter with damma or with sukun, except the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And they have made for Him a portion from His servants﴾ [[Verse 15 of surah al-Zukhruf; see vol. 16, p. 69.]] [al-Zukhruf: 15], for a reason mentioned earlier. Hafs read kufuwan with a damma on the fa' and without hamzah. All of them are eloquent dialects.

**The discussion of the hadiths reported concerning the virtues of this surah. It has three issues.**

**The first issue:** It is established in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that a man heard another man reciting (Say: He is Allah, the One) repeatedly. When morning came, he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and the man had been regarding it as little [[That is, he considered it small in reward for the effort, not as belittling it.]]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an." And from him (Abu Sa'id) he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Can any one of you not manage to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night?" That was hard for them, and they said: "Which of us can manage that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge [[In the commentary of al-Ayni on al-Bukhari, in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an: his words "Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge" are a metaphor for "Say: He is Allah, One."]] is a third of the Qur'an." Muslim narrated it, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', with the same meaning.

And he (Muslim) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gather [[From the verb meaning to kill and to strike; it is used both transitively and intransitively.]], for I am going to recite to you a third of the Qur'an." So those who gathered gathered [[That is, whoever came together came together.]]. Then the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came out and recited (Say: He is Allah, One), then went back in. Some of us said to others: "I think this is news that came to him from the heavens, and that is what brought him in." Then he came out and said: "I told you I would recite to you a third of the Qur'an. Indeed, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an."

Some scholars said: It is equal to a third of the Qur'an because of this name, which is "the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad)," for it is not found in any other surah. The same applies to "One (Ahad)." It has also been said: The Qur'an was revealed in three parts: one third of it is rulings, one third is promise and threat, and one third is names and attributes. (Say: He is Allah, One) combines [[An addition from al-Khatib.]] the names and attributes, and nothing else. This interpretation is supported by what is in the Sahih of Muslim, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, divided the Qur'an into three parts, and made (Say: He is Allah, One) one of the parts of the Qur'an." This is an explicit text, and with this meaning the surah was named Surat al-Ikhlas (the Sincerity). And Allah knows best.

**The second issue:** Muslim narrated from A'isha that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man in command of a detachment, and he used to recite to his companions in their prayer, and he would end with (Say: He is Allah, One). When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Ask him why he does that." They asked him, and he said: "Because it is the attribute of the Most Merciful, so I love to recite it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tell him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves him."

And al-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A man from the Ansar used to lead them in prayer at the mosque of Quba'. Whenever he began a surah which he recited to them in the prayer, he would begin with (Say: He is Allah, One), until he finished it, then recite another surah along with it. He did this in every rak'ah. His companions spoke to him and said: "You recite this surah, then you do not seem to think it suffices you until you recite another surah. Either recite it alone, or leave it and recite another surah." He said: "I will not abandon it. If you like, I will lead you with it, and if you dislike it, I will leave you." They regarded him as the best of them, and they disliked that anyone other than him should lead them. When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, they told him the news. He said: "O so-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions command you? And what makes you recite this surah in every rak'ah?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its love has admitted you into Paradise."

He (al-Tirmidhi) said: A hadith that is hasan gharib sahih. Ibn al-Arabi said: "This is evidence that it is permissible to repeat a surah in every rak'ah. I saw at the Gate of the Tribes, near it, an imam from among the twenty-eight imams who used to lead the Tarawih prayers in Ramadan for the Turks. In every rak'ah he would recite (Al-hamdu lillah) and (Say: He is Allah, One), until he completed the Tarawih, to lighten it for them and out of desire for its virtue. And it is not from the Sunnah to complete the Qur'an in Ramadan."

I say: This is the text of Malik's statement. Malik said: "Completing the Qur'an in the mosques is not a Sunnah."

**The third issue:** Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas [[The narration in al-Tirmidhi is from Abu Hurayrah.]] ibn Malik, who said: I was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he heard a man reciting (Say: He is Allah, One). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is due (wajabat)." I said: "What is due?" He said: "Paradise." He said: This is a hadith hasan sahih [[In al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib.]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq al-Basri narrated to us, who said: Hatim ibn Maymun Abu Sahl narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) two hundred times every day, his sins for fifty years will be erased, except for a debt that is upon him." And by this same chain from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever wants to sleep on his bed, and sleeps on his right side, then recites (Say: He is Allah, One) one hundred times, on the Day of Resurrection the Lord will say: 'O My servant, enter Paradise by your right side.'" He said: This is a gharib hadith from the hadith of Thabit from Anas.

In the Musnad of Abu Muhammad al-Darimi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) fifty times, the sins of fifty years will be forgiven him." He said: And Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, who said: Haywah narrated to us, who said: Abu Aqil informed me that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) ten times, a palace will be built for him in Paradise. Whoever recites it twenty times, two palaces will be built for him in Paradise by it. Whoever recites it thirty times, three palaces will be built for him in Paradise by it." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, then we will certainly multiply our palaces!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more expansive than that." Abu Muhammad said: Abu Aqil is Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, and they claimed that he was one of the Abdal [[The Abdal are a category of righteous people in Sufi and popular belief.]].

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz mentioned, from the hadith of Abu al-'Ala' Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) during the illness in which he dies, he will not be tested in his grave, he will be safe from the squeezing of the grave, and the angels will carry him on the Day of Resurrection on their palms, until they convey him across the Sirat to Paradise." He said: This is a gharib hadith from the hadith of Yazid, narrated alone by Nasr ibn Hammad al-Bajali.

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Thabit al-Hafiz mentioned, from Isa ibn Abi Fatimah al-Razi, who said: I heard Malik ibn Anas say: "When the bell is struck, the anger of the Most Merciful intensifies, so the angels descend and take hold of the regions of the earth, and they never stop reciting (Say: He is Allah, One) until His anger, Mighty and Majestic, subsides."

And he (Ibn Thabit) extracted, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters the mosque on Friday and prays four rak'ahs, reciting in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and (Say: He is Allah, One) fifty times, that makes two hundred times in four rak'ahs. He will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him."

Abu Umar, the client of Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, said, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) when he enters his house, it drives poverty away from the people of that house and from the neighbours."

And from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) once, will be blessed. Whoever recites it twice, will be blessed and so will his family. Whoever recites it three times, will be blessed and so will all his neighbours. Whoever recites it twelve times, Allah will build for him twelve palaces in Paradise, and the guardian angels will say: 'Come, let us look at the palace of our brother.' If he recites it one hundred times, Allah will expiate for him the sins of fifty years, except for bloodshed and wealth. If he recites it four hundred times, Allah will expiate for him the sins of one hundred years. If he recites it a thousand times, he will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him."

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: A man complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of poverty and the straitness of his livelihood. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "When you enter the house, greet [anyone in it] if there is someone in it, and if there is no one in it, greet me, and recite (Say: He is Allah, One) once." The man did so, and Allah made provision abundant for him, to the point that his neighbours were showered with it.

And Anas said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Tabuk, when the sun rose white, with a ray and a light, which I had never seen rise like that before. Jibril came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O Jibril, why do I see the sun rising white with a ray which I have never seen it rise like that before?" He said: "That is because Mu'awiyah ibn Mu'awiyah al-Laythi died in Madinah today, and Allah sent seventy thousand angels to pray over him." He [the Prophet] said: "And for what reason?" He said: "He used to recite (Say: He is Allah, One) abundantly, in the hours of the night and the hours of the day, and in his walking, his standing and his sitting. So, O Messenger of Allah, would you like me to fold the earth for you, so that you may pray over him?" He said: "Yes." So he prayed over him, then returned.

This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi, and Allah knows best.

Some of us said to others: "I think this is news that came to him from the heavens, and that is what brought him in." Then he came out and said: "I told you I would recite to you a third of the Qur'an. Indeed, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an."

It has also been said: The Qur'an was revealed in three parts: one third of it is rulings, one third is promise and threat, and one third is names and attributes. When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Ask him why he does that." They asked him, and he said: "Because it is the attribute of the Most Merciful, so I love to recite it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tell him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves him."

And al-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A man from the Ansar used to lead them in prayer at the mosque of Quba'. Whenever he began a surah which he recited to them in the prayer, he would begin with (Say: He is Allah, One), until he finished it, then recite another surah along with it. Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 112, verse 1–4 (part 1 of 2):

The surah "al-Ikhlas" is Meccan according to Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah and Jabir. It is Medinan according to one of the two opinions attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, and to Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. It has four verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten.﴾ ﴿And there is none comparable to Him.﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One (aḥad)﴾, meaning the One, the Single, who has no likeness, no equal, no consort, no child and no partner. The root of aḥad is waḥad; the waw was changed into a hamzah. From this is the saying of al-Nabighah [[The first half of the line, as in his mu'allaqah:
kaʼanna rahli wa-qad zāla al-nahāru bina
and dhu al-Jalil is a place where al-Jalil grows, and al-Jalil is al-thumam. Al-thumam is a weak, short plant that does not grow tall.]]:

*bi-dhi al-Jalil ʿalā mustaʾnisin waḥadi*

The difference between wāḥid and aḥad has already been discussed in surah al-Baqarah, and it is also fully treated in the book "al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna". All praise is due to Allah. Aḥad is in the nominative, meaning: He is aḥad. It has also been said that the meaning is: Say: The matter and affair is: Allah is aḥad. It has also been said that aḥad is a substitute (badal) for the word Allah. A group of readers read (aḥadun Allahu) without tanwin, seeking lightness and to avoid the meeting of two unvoweled letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). From this is the saying of the poet:

*wa-la dhakira Allaha illa qalilan*

This is the second half of a line by Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali. Its first half is:

*fa-alfaythu ghayra mustaʿtibin*

﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge (al-samad)﴾, meaning the One to whom one turns (yusmadu ilayhi) in needs. This is what al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The One to whom one turns in needs," as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [[Verse 53 of surah al-Nahl.]] [al-Nahl: 53]. The lexicographers said: al-samad is the lord (sayyid) to whom one turns in calamities and needs. He said:

*alā bakkara al-nāʿī bi-khayri [[It is narrated as "bi-khayri", and that is the correct reading, because after it he mentions two people.]] banī Asad ... bi-ʿAmr ibn Mas'ud wa-bi-l-sayyid al-samad*

Some people said: al-samad is the one who endures and remains, who has not ceased and will not cease. It has also been said: its explanation is what follows it: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten.﴾ Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: al-samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will die, and everything that dies is inherited. Ali, Ibn 'Abbas also, Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah and Sufyan said: al-samad is the lord (sayyid) whose lordship has reached its completion in all kinds of nobility and lordship. From this is the saying of the poet:

*ʿalawtahu bi-ḥusāmin thumma qultu lahu ... khudhhā Ḥudhayf fa-anta al-sayyid al-samad*

Abu Hurayrah said: it is the One who is free of need of every creature, and every creature is in need of Him. al-Suddi said: it is the One sought in desires and the One sought for help in calamities. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the One who does what He wills and decrees what He desires. Muqatil said: it is the Perfect, in whom there is no defect, and from this is the saying of al-Zibriqan:

*sirū jamīʿan bi-niṣfi al-layli wa-iʿtamadū ... wa-lā rahīnata illā sayyidun ṣamadu*

al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Jubayr said: al-samad is the solid (al-muṣmat) which has no hollow (jawf) [[This is not permissible for Allah, the Exalted.]]. The poet said:

*shihābu ḥurūbin lā tuzālu jiyāduhu ... ʿawābisa yaʿlukna al-shakīma al-muṣammadā [[ʿalaka al-dābbatu al-lijām yaʿlukuhu (from the pattern qatala) ʿalkan: she chewed it and moved it. The kashīm and shakīmah: the iron bar across the horse's mouth.]]*

I say: We have already presented these opinions explained in the discussion of al-samad in "al-Asna", and that the correct one among them is what the derivation (ishtiqaq) supports, which is the first opinion, mentioned by al-Khattabi. Whoever Allah has removed far away and disgraced, and whose abode and dwelling He has made the Fire, has dropped from this surah, and he recited "Allah, the One, the Eternal" in the prayer while people were listening, so he dropped "Say: He is", and claimed that it is not part of the Qur'an. He altered the wording of aḥad and claimed that this is the correct version, while what the people hold is falsehood and absurdity, thereby nullifying the meaning of the verse. The people of tafsir said: the verse was revealed as an answer to the polytheists when they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Describe your Lord for us: is He of gold, or of copper, or of brass?" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, responded to them: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ So in "He is" there is an indication of the place of the response and the location of the answer. When it is dropped, the meaning of the verse collapses, and the fabrication against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the denial of His Messenger ﷺ, become valid. al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the polytheists said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Give us the lineage of your Lord," so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ And al-samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will die, and everything that dies will be inherited, whereas Allah, the Exalted, does not die and is not inherited. ﴿And there is none comparable to Him (kufuwan aḥad)﴾ [[Reading with the hamzah is the reading of Nafi', and it is the reading of the author.]]: He said: there is no likeness to Him and no equal, and there is nothing like unto Him. He said: Jibril then brought him this surah, "Say: He is Allah, the One," and he mentioned something similar, but he did not mention from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and this is more sound, as al-Tirmidhi said. I say: In this hadith there is confirmation of the wording "Say: He is Allah, the One" and the explanation of al-samad, which has already been mentioned. Something similar is narrated from 'Ikrimah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He begets not" as Maryam gave birth, "nor is He begotten" as 'Isa and 'Uzayr were begotten. This is a refutation of the Christians and of those who say: 'Uzayr is the son of Allah.

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz mentioned, from the hadith of Abu al-'Ala' Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) during the illness in which he dies, he will not be tested in his grave, he will be safe from the squeezing of the grave, and the angels will carry him on the Day of Resurrection on their palms, until they convey him across the Sirat to Paradise." He said: This is a gharib hadith from the hadith of Yazid, narrated alone by Nasr ibn Hammad al-Bajali.

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Thabit al-Hafiz mentioned, from Isa ibn Abi Fatimah al-Razi, who said: I heard Malik ibn Anas say: "When the bell is struck, the anger of the Most Merciful intensifies, so the angels descend and take hold of the regions of the earth, and they never stop reciting (Say: He is Allah, One) until His anger, Mighty and Majestic, subsides."

And he (Ibn Thabit) extracted, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters the mosque on Friday and prays four rak'ahs, reciting in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and (Say: He is Allah, One) fifty times, that makes two hundred times in four rak'ahs. He will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him."

Abu Umar, the client of Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, said, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) when he enters his house, it drives poverty away from the people of that house and from the neighbours."

And from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) once, will be blessed. Whoever recites it twice, will be blessed and so will his family. Whoever recites it three times, will be blessed and so will all his neighbours. Whoever recites it twelve times, Allah will build for him twelve palaces in Paradise, and the guardian angels will say: 'Come, let us look at the palace of our brother.' If he recites it one hundred times, Allah will expiate for him the sins of fifty years, except for bloodshed and wealth. If he recites it four hundred times, Allah will expiate for him the sins of one hundred years. If he recites it a thousand times, he will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him."

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: A man complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of poverty and the straitness of his livelihood. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "When you enter the house, greet [anyone in it] if there is someone in it, and if there is no one in it, greet me, and recite (Say: He is Allah, One) once." The man did so, and Allah made provision abundant for him, to the point that his neighbours were showered with it.

And Anas said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Tabuk, when the sun rose white, with a ray and a light, which I had never seen rise like that before. Jibril came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O Jibril, why do I see the sun rising white with a ray which I have never seen it rise like that before?" He said: "That is because Mu'awiyah ibn Mu'awiyah al-Laythi died in Madinah today, and Allah sent seventy thousand angels to pray over him." He [the Prophet] said: "And for what reason?" He said: "He used to recite (Say: He is Allah, One) abundantly, in the hours of the night and the hours of the day, and in his walking, his standing and his sitting. So, O Messenger of Allah, would you like me to fold the earth for you, so that you may pray over him?" He said: "Yes." So he prayed over him, then returned.

This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 112, verse 1–4 (part 1 of 2):

The surah "al-Ikhlas" is Meccan according to Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah and Jabir. It is Medinan according to one of the two opinions attributed to Ibn 'Abbas, and to Qatadah, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi. It has four verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten.﴾ ﴿And there is none comparable to Him.﴾

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One (aḥad)﴾, meaning the One, the Single, who has no likeness, no equal, no consort, no child and no partner. The root of aḥad is waḥad; the waw was changed into a hamzah. From this is the saying of al-Nabighah [[The first half of the line, as in his mu'allaqah:
kaʼanna rahli wa-qad zāla al-nahāru bina
and dhu al-Jalil is a place where al-Jalil grows, and al-Jalil is al-thumam. Al-thumam is a weak, short plant that does not grow tall.]]:

*bi-dhi al-Jalil ʿalā mustaʾnisin waḥadi*

The difference between wāḥid and aḥad has already been discussed in surah al-Baqarah, and it is also fully treated in the book "al-Asna fi Sharh Asma' Allah al-Husna". All praise is due to Allah. Aḥad is in the nominative, meaning: He is aḥad. It has also been said that the meaning is: Say: The matter and affair is: Allah is aḥad. It has also been said that aḥad is a substitute (badal) for the word Allah. A group of readers read (aḥadun Allahu) without tanwin, seeking lightness and to avoid the meeting of two unvoweled letters (iltiqa' al-sakinayn). From this is the saying of the poet:

*wa-la dhakira Allaha illa qalilan*

This is the second half of a line by Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali. Its first half is:

*fa-alfaythu ghayra mustaʿtibin*

﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge (al-samad)﴾, meaning the One to whom one turns (yusmadu ilayhi) in needs. This is what al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The One to whom one turns in needs," as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help﴾ [[Verse 53 of surah al-Nahl.]] [al-Nahl: 53]. The lexicographers said: al-samad is the lord (sayyid) to whom one turns in calamities and needs. He said:

*alā bakkara al-nāʿī bi-khayri [[It is narrated as "bi-khayri", and that is the correct reading, because after it he mentions two people.]] banī Asad ... bi-ʿAmr ibn Mas'ud wa-bi-l-sayyid al-samad*

Some people said: al-samad is the one who endures and remains, who has not ceased and will not cease. It has also been said: its explanation is what follows it: ﴿He begets not, nor is He begotten.﴾ Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: al-samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will die, and everything that dies is inherited. Ali, Ibn 'Abbas also, Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah and Sufyan said: al-samad is the lord (sayyid) whose lordship has reached its completion in all kinds of nobility and lordship. From this is the saying of the poet:

*ʿalawtahu bi-ḥusāmin thumma qultu lahu ... khudhhā Ḥudhayf fa-anta al-sayyid al-samad*

Abu Hurayrah said: it is the One who is free of need of every creature, and every creature is in need of Him. al-Suddi said: it is the One sought in desires and the One sought for help in calamities. al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: it is the One who does what He wills and decrees what He desires. Muqatil said: it is the Perfect, in whom there is no defect, and from this is the saying of al-Zibriqan:

*sirū jamīʿan bi-niṣfi al-layli wa-iʿtamadū ... wa-lā rahīnata illā sayyidun ṣamadu*

al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Ibn Jubayr said: al-samad is the solid (al-muṣmat) which has no hollow (jawf) [[This is not permissible for Allah, the Exalted.]]. The poet said:

*shihābu ḥurūbin lā tuzālu jiyāduhu ... ʿawābisa yaʿlukna al-shakīma al-muṣammadā [[ʿalaka al-dābbatu al-lijām yaʿlukuhu (from the pattern qatala) ʿalkan: she chewed it and moved it. The kashīm and shakīmah: the iron bar across the horse's mouth.]]*

I say: We have already presented these opinions explained in the discussion of al-samad in "al-Asna", and that the correct one among them is what the derivation (ishtiqaq) supports, which is the first opinion, mentioned by al-Khattabi. Whoever Allah has removed far away and disgraced, and whose abode and dwelling He has made the Fire, has dropped from this surah, and he recited "Allah, the One, the Eternal" in the prayer while people were listening, so he dropped "Say: He is", and claimed that it is not part of the Qur'an. He altered the wording of aḥad and claimed that this is the correct version, while what the people hold is falsehood and absurdity, thereby nullifying the meaning of the verse. The people of tafsir said: the verse was revealed as an answer to the polytheists when they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Describe your Lord for us: is He of gold, or of copper, or of brass?" Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, responded to them: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ So in "He is" there is an indication of the place of the response and the location of the answer. When it is dropped, the meaning of the verse collapses, and the fabrication against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the denial of His Messenger ﷺ, become valid. al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the polytheists said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Give us the lineage of your Lord," so Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge.﴾ And al-samad is the One who neither begets nor is begotten, because everything that is begotten will die, and everything that dies will be inherited, whereas Allah, the Exalted, does not die and is not inherited. ﴿And there is none comparable to Him (kufuwan aḥad)﴾ [[Reading with the hamzah is the reading of Nafi', and it is the reading of the author.]]: He said: there is no likeness to Him and no equal, and there is nothing like unto Him. It is narrated from Abu al-'Aliyah that the Prophet ﷺ mentioned their gods, and they said: "Give us the lineage of your Lord." He said: Jibril then brought him this surah, "Say: He is Allah, the One," and he mentioned something similar, but he did not mention from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and this is more sound, as al-Tirmidhi said. I say: In this hadith there is confirmation of the wording "Say: He is Allah, the One" and the explanation of al-samad, which has already been mentioned. Something similar is narrated from 'Ikrimah. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He begets not" as Maryam gave birth, "nor is He begotten" as 'Isa and 'Uzayr were begotten. This is a refutation of the Christians and of those who say: 'Uzayr is the son of Allah.

﴿And there is none comparable to Him (wa-lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad)﴾, meaning: there was never anyone like Him, any equal. There is inversion (taqdim wa-ta'khir) in it; its estimated form is: "wa-lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad," and he placed the predicate of kana before its subject so that the endings of the verses would follow one pattern. Kufuwan is also read with a damma on the fa' and with sukun. It has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah that every noun of three letters whose first letter is vowelled with damma may have the middle letter with damma or with sukun, except the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And they have made for Him a portion from His servants﴾ [[Verse 15 of surah al-Zukhruf; see vol. 16, p. 69.]] [al-Zukhruf: 15], for a reason mentioned earlier. Hafs read kufuwan with a damma on the fa' and without hamzah. All of them are eloquent dialects.

**The discussion of the hadiths reported concerning the virtues of this surah. It has three issues.**

**The first issue:** It is established in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that a man heard another man reciting (Say: He is Allah, the One) repeatedly. When morning came, he went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and the man had been regarding it as little [[That is, he considered it small in reward for the effort, not as belittling it.]]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an." And from him (Abu Sa'id) he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Can any one of you not manage to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night?" That was hard for them, and they said: "Which of us can manage that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge [[In the commentary of al-Ayni on al-Bukhari, in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an: his words "Allah, the One, the Eternal Refuge" are a metaphor for "Say: He is Allah, One."]] is a third of the Qur'an." Muslim narrated it, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', with the same meaning.

And he (Muslim) narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gather [[From the verb meaning to kill and to strike; it is used both transitively and intransitively.]], for I am going to recite to you a third of the Qur'an." So those who gathered gathered [[That is, whoever came together came together.]]. Then the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) came out and recited (Say: He is Allah, One), then went back in. Some of us said to others: "I think this is news that came to him from the heavens, and that is what brought him in." Then he came out and said: "I told you I would recite to you a third of the Qur'an. Indeed, it is equal to a third of the Qur'an."

Some scholars said: It is equal to a third of the Qur'an because of this name, which is "the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad)," for it is not found in any other surah. The same applies to "One (Ahad)." It has also been said: The Qur'an was revealed in three parts: one third of it is rulings, one third is promise and threat, and one third is names and attributes. (Say: He is Allah, One) combines [[An addition from al-Khatib.]] the names and attributes, and nothing else. This interpretation is supported by what is in the Sahih of Muslim, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, divided the Qur'an into three parts, and made (Say: He is Allah, One) one of the parts of the Qur'an." This is an explicit text, and with this meaning the surah was named Surat al-Ikhlas (the Sincerity). And Allah knows best.

**The second issue:** Muslim narrated from A'isha that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man in command of a detachment, and he used to recite to his companions in their prayer, and he would end with (Say: He is Allah, One). When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Ask him why he does that." They asked him, and he said: "Because it is the attribute of the Most Merciful, so I love to recite it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Tell him that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves him."

And al-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas ibn Malik, who said: A man from the Ansar used to lead them in prayer at the mosque of Quba'. Whenever he began a surah which he recited to them in the prayer, he would begin with (Say: He is Allah, One), until he finished it, then recite another surah along with it. He did this in every rak'ah. His companions spoke to him and said: "You recite this surah, then you do not seem to think it suffices you until you recite another surah. Either recite it alone, or leave it and recite another surah." He said: "I will not abandon it. If you like, I will lead you with it, and if you dislike it, I will leave you." They regarded him as the best of them, and they disliked that anyone other than him should lead them. When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, they told him the news. He said: "O so-and-so, what prevents you from doing what your companions command you? And what makes you recite this surah in every rak'ah?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Its love has admitted you into Paradise."

He (al-Tirmidhi) said: A hadith that is hasan gharib sahih. Ibn al-Arabi said: "This is evidence that it is permissible to repeat a surah in every rak'ah. I saw at the Gate of the Tribes, near it, an imam from among the twenty-eight imams who used to lead the Tarawih prayers in Ramadan for the Turks. In every rak'ah he would recite (Al-hamdu lillah) and (Say: He is Allah, One), until he completed the Tarawih, to lighten it for them and out of desire for its virtue. And it is not from the Sunnah to complete the Qur'an in Ramadan."

I say: This is the text of Malik's statement. Malik said: "Completing the Qur'an in the mosques is not a Sunnah."

**The third issue:** Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Anas [[The narration in al-Tirmidhi is from Abu Hurayrah.]] ibn Malik, who said: I was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he heard a man reciting (Say: He is Allah, One). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is due (wajabat)." I said: "What is due?" He said: "Paradise." He said: This is a hadith hasan sahih [[In al-Tirmidhi: hasan gharib.]].

Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Marzuq al-Basri narrated to us, who said: Hatim ibn Maymun Abu Sahl narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) two hundred times every day, his sins for fifty years will be erased, except for a debt that is upon him." And by this same chain from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever wants to sleep on his bed, and sleeps on his right side, then recites (Say: He is Allah, One) one hundred times, on the Day of Resurrection the Lord will say: 'O My servant, enter Paradise by your right side.'" He said: This is a gharib hadith from the hadith of Thabit from Anas.

In the Musnad of Abu Muhammad al-Darimi, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) fifty times, the sins of fifty years will be forgiven him." He said: And Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, who said: Haywah narrated to us, who said: Abu Aqil informed me that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) ten times, a palace will be built for him in Paradise. Whoever recites it twenty times, two palaces will be built for him in Paradise by it. Whoever recites it thirty times, three palaces will be built for him in Paradise by it." Then Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, then we will certainly multiply our palaces!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah is more expansive than that." Abu Muhammad said: Abu Aqil is Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, and they claimed that he was one of the Abdal [[The Abdal are a category of righteous people in Sufi and popular belief.]].

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz mentioned, from the hadith of Abu al-'Ala' Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) during the illness in which he dies, he will not be tested in his grave, he will be safe from the squeezing of the grave, and the angels will carry him on the Day of Resurrection on their palms, until they convey him across the Sirat to Paradise." He said: This is a gharib hadith from the hadith of Yazid, narrated alone by Nasr ibn Hammad al-Bajali.

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Thabit al-Hafiz mentioned, from Isa ibn Abi Fatimah al-Razi, who said: I heard Malik ibn Anas say: "When the bell is struck, the anger of the Most Merciful intensifies, so the angels descend and take hold of the regions of the earth, and they never stop reciting (Say: He is Allah, One) until His anger, Mighty and Majestic, subsides."

And he (Ibn Thabit) extracted, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi, from Malik, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever enters the mosque on Friday and prays four rak'ahs, reciting in each rak'ah the Opening of the Book and (Say: He is Allah, One) fifty times, that makes two hundred times in four rak'ahs. He will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him."

Abu Umar, the client of Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, said, from Jarir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) when he enters his house, it drives poverty away from the people of that house and from the neighbours."

And from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites (Say: He is Allah, One) once, will be blessed. Whoever recites it twice, will be blessed and so will his family. Whoever recites it three times, will be blessed and so will all his neighbours. Whoever recites it twelve times, Allah will build for him twelve palaces in Paradise, and the guardian angels will say: 'Come, let us look at the palace of our brother.' If he recites it one hundred times, Allah will expiate for him the sins of fifty years, except for bloodshed and wealth. If he recites it four hundred times, Allah will expiate for him the sins of one hundred years. If he recites it a thousand times, he will not die until he sees his place in Paradise, or it is shown to him."

And from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: A man complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of poverty and the straitness of his livelihood. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "When you enter the house, greet [anyone in it] if there is someone in it, and if there is no one in it, greet me, and recite (Say: He is Allah, One) once." The man did so, and Allah made provision abundant for him, to the point that his neighbours were showered with it.

And Anas said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Tabuk, when the sun rose white, with a ray and a light, which I had never seen rise like that before. Jibril came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "O Jibril, why do I see the sun rising white with a ray which I have never seen it rise like that before?" He said: "That is because Mu'awiyah ibn Mu'awiyah al-Laythi died in Madinah today, and Allah sent seventy thousand angels to pray over him." He [the Prophet] said: "And for what reason?" He said: "He used to recite (Say: He is Allah, One) abundantly, in the hours of the night and the hours of the day, and in his walking, his standing and his sitting. So, O Messenger of Allah, would you like me to fold the earth for you, so that you may pray over him?" He said: "Yes." So he prayed over him, then returned.

This was mentioned by al-Tha'labi, and Allah knows best.
